choose.lead: What is this device going to be used for?

master.title: Game master
master.text: For your phone, tablet or laptop: create and manage quizzes, start and run games, grade answers. Only one device is in control at a time.

screen.title: Screen
screen.text: For the TV or projector that everyone sees: shows questions, images, videos and the scores. There can be any number of screens, also several browser windows on the same device.

devBoard.title: Virtual dev board
devBoard.text: For development only: press buzzers with a mouse click, without a real BuzzerBox.

guide.title: How to start a game

connect.title: Connect.
connect.text: Connect each device to the WiFi {{wifi}} and open {{address}} in the browser. That takes you to this page.

screen.title: Set up the screen.
screen.text: A display on the HDMI port of the BuzzerBox shows the screen by itself. For each further screen, open this page in a browser window of its own and choose “Screen”.
screen.tip: A laptop can be game master and screen at the same time. Open a second browser window, choose “Screen” there and move it to the projector or TV (best in full screen with F11). This also gives you several screens on one device, one per window.

master.title: Take control.
master.text: Choose “Game master” on your device, in a window of its own if it is a screen as well. You connect wireless buzzers on the game master's home page by plugging them into the BuzzerBox over USB and tapping “Adopt”.

quiz.title: Choose a quiz.
quiz.text: “New game” starts a stored quiz from the beginning, “Continue game” carries on with a savegame. No quiz yet? Create or import one under “Manage games”.

teams.title: Set up the teams.
teams.text: Give each team a buzzer, choose the look of the screen and tap “Start game”.

play.title: Play.
play.text: When a team presses its buzzer, all others are locked, and you grade the answer with “Correct” or “Wrong”. After “Wrong”, the others may buzz again. “Next question” moves on, and after the last question “End game” does.

guide.hint: The game is saved all the time. If a device reloads or loses the WiFi for a moment, it carries on at the same point afterwards.

boxSettings.title: BuzzerBox settings
boxSettings.unavailable: This server has no BuzzerBox settings.
boxSettings.intro: From the file buzzerbox.txt on the memory card's boot partition. The box applies them every time it starts.
boxSettings.restarting: The BuzzerBox is restarting, which takes about a minute.
boxSettings.restartingConnect: Then connect to the WiFi “{{wifi}}” and open {{address}}.
boxSettings.restartingReconnect: This page reconnects by itself afterwards.
boxSettings.saved: Saved. The changes apply from the BuzzerBox's next start.

boxSettings.defaultHint: The file doesn't set this value itself
boxSettings.invalidInFile: “{{value}}” in the file is invalid, so the default applies.
boxSettings.ethernetInWifiNetwork: Must be in a different network from the WiFi address.
boxSettings.editingWarning: If the WiFi or the address changes, all devices are disconnected after the restart and have to connect again.
boxSettings.readOnly: To change them, put the memory card into a computer and edit buzzerbox.txt. With {{editKey}}=true in the file, the settings can be changed here as well.

confirmLeave.title: Discard the changes?
confirmLeave.message: The changed settings haven't been saved yet.

WIFI_PASSPHRASE.label: Password
WIFI_PASSPHRASE.hint: 8 to 63 characters, no umlauts or other special letters

WIFI_COUNTRY_CODE.label: Country
WIFI_COUNTRY_CODE.hint: Two letters, e.g. DE, AT or CH. It decides which channels are allowed.

WIFI_ANTENNA.label: Antenna
WIFI_ANTENNA.hint: Only the Compute Module 4 has the external antenna.

ANALOG_BUZZERS.label: Analog buzzers
ANALOG_BUZZERS.hint: Buzzers plugged into the box's sockets. Without them, the box offers only the wireless buzzers.

SERVER_IP_ADDRESS.label: WiFi address
SERVER_IP_ADDRESS.hint: Devices get the addresses .50 to .150 of the same network.

ETHERNET_IP_ADDRESS.label: Ethernet address
ETHERNET_IP_ADDRESS.hint: For a laptop on a cable; in a different network from the WiFi.

SERVER_HOSTNAMES.label: Names of the box
SERVER_HOSTNAMES.hint: The box can be opened under these names, separated by spaces.

SCREEN_MODE.label: TV resolution
SCREEN_MODE.hint: If the TV doesn't offer the resolution, it chooses one itself. A Raspberry Pi 4 can't play 4K at 60 Hz smoothly.

TOUCH_DISPLAY.label: Touchscreen
TOUCH_DISPLAY.hint: With the touchscreen, the box shows the game master's controls on it.

TOUCH_DISPLAY_ROTATION.label: Rotate the touch display
TOUCH_DISPLAY_ROTATION.hint: Yes turns the picture upside down, in case the touchscreen is built in the other way round.

TOUCH_DISPLAY_SCALE.label: Size on the touch display
TOUCH_DISPLAY_SCALE.hint: How large the game master's controls appear on the touch display.

ssh.title: SSH access
ssh.editingNote: Keys apply as soon as they are added or removed. “Save” and “Cancel” don't affect them.
ssh.intro: From buzzerbox-ssh-keys.txt on the boot partition. With one of these keys, you can log in as {{user}} and manage the box with sudo: ssh {{user}}@{{address}}.
ssh.notActiveYet: Applies from the box's next start.
ssh.private: This is a private key, which never belongs on the box. Use the content of the file ending in .pub.
ssh.notAKey: Not a public SSH key. It starts with e.g. ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa.
ssh.addHint: The content of a .pub file, e.g. ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub. Applies right away.
